note: The Studio (docs/spec/05 §6). Generated by tools/content/devcut.ts. Captions are NEW placards (source 'reconstructed'); every fact cites docs/secrets.md, the spec, or the original file. No personal details beyond the credits and file metadata. The PrintOMatic licence key is deliberately redacted.

intro.text: The people who made Go West!, set the way the game listed them.
Names, dates and folders the team left in the files, read the way an archivist reads a margin.
One telegram, one name, and the first storm.
Pictures that were drawn, finished and put away. Click one to look closer.
Voices and sounds that were recorded but never played. Some have not been listened to yet, and say so.
Everything the Developer's Cut brings back, with where it lived and how much of it is new.
The developers' own tools, dusted off.

curatorNote.text: Go West! The Homesteader's Challenge was made in 1995–96 by Edunetics and published by Brighter Child, developed in conjunction with the Plano Independent School District, Plano, Texas. These are the people the game credits.

traces.title: The movie inside the program
traces.caption: Before Longview, before the login, there is a small movie you never really see. It lives inside GOWEST.EXE itself, and its only job is to look over your computer: enough colours, a sound card, Video for Windows, QuickTime, a MIDI device. Then it plays the Edunetics logo and steps aside. Hold Shift on a fatal warning and the Quit button quietly turns into Continue.

facts.text: Embedded RIFX movie at file offset 729830, 144,284 bytes; decompiled with ProjectorRays and cited as EXE:<script>.
Checks colour depth, sound, Video for Windows 1.1, QuickTime 2.0 and MIDI (the MIDI check is the only non-vital one).
Vital dialogs: holding Shift swaps Quit for Continue. Non-vital dialogs can write WIN.INI [GOWEST] <label>=1 to stay silent next time.
The logo is EDULOGO.MOV, 10.8 s. The EXE also names EDULOGO.MOVULOGO.AVI, perhaps a lost AVI version.
Its message text keeps a typo: "In order ro run this program".
GOWEST.EXE is dated 6 March 1996, so the projector was never rebuilt after the June movie edits.

traces.title: ECOSIM, SECO and SVIVOT
traces.caption: Every studio has names for things before the box art does. Go West! was ECOSIM, an economic simulation, and SECO on the build server. The whole tree lived under a folder called SVIVOT, Hebrew for "environments". The names are still baked into the files, in paths like M:\SVIVOT\SECO\PROGRAM\DATA\QT\INTRO.

facts.text: Paths baked into the movies: M:\SVIVOT\SECO\PROGRAM\DATA\QT\INTRO, P:\ECOSIM\PROGRAM\GOWEST.DIR, Q:\ECOSIM\PROGRAM\DATA\PICT\NEWS\NEWS1\18873.PCT.
The sound names ECONOM*, ECO0xx and ECONOO13 match the ECOSIM codename.
SVIVOT (סביבות) means "environments".
set g_path to "p:\ecosim\" is hard-coded in BANK09/MovieScript 15.ls:25.

traces.title: stam
traces.caption: A throwaway variable named with a Hebrew word that means "just" or "whatever". It turns up in the names table of ten movies, a small trace of the everyday talk of the people who made the game.

facts.text: stam (סתם) is in the Lnam of ALBUM, BANK09, BHOUSE1, CALEND, FIELD, HOUSE1-3, TSTREET1 and TTALK.

traces.title: Car, video, oven
traces.caption: Line 11 of the 1880 save template still reads car, video, oven. A video player on the Kansas prairie suggests the save layout came from an earlier, modern-day economics simulation. In the game, the slots became a car, a Kodak camera and a cooking stove.

facts.text: SHARED/3003-Propet line 11 and CALEND/1565-IPropet: 11,0,0,0,car,video,oven. The same template has the labels "Check plot" and "Buisness".

traces.title: NewForRaz
traces.caption: A one-call shortcut for starting a fresh game, made for a programmer who needed to test the farm without sitting through the stagecoach ride. Nothing in the shipped game ever calls it. Its twin, SaveForRaz, was deleted; only its name survives in the symbol table.

facts.text: SHARED/MovieScript 3286: puts 0 into line 2 and 1 into line 1 of field "Begin", calls NewStart(), newGame(), Always(), and sets g_IntroReturn to "Start".
SaveForRaz appears only in the SHARED names table.

traces.title: The Option key at the door
traces.caption: The login screen only accepts eight ordinary characters for a user ID. Hold Option or Alt and the filter steps aside: any character, any length.

facts.text: LOGIN/CastScript 42 - txtUserID: on keyDown, the whitelist and the 8-character limit run only when not (the optionDown). The ID becomes a folder name under C:\EDU\USERS\.

traces.title: Tools left on the bench
traces.caption: Finished games still carry the tools that built them. Here a debug switch is wired permanently off, a stopwatch times each month, a test page tries its best to print, and a handler waits to play an animation from a network drive the disc never had.

facts.text: DEBUG() is hard-wired off: INTRO sets fIsDebug to 0; LOGIN's gDEBUG is only ever set to 0.
ALBUM/MovieScript 27 on ppp prints "I try to print" in Helvetica italic beside a rounded rectangle.
CALEND/ScoreScript 197 puts the timer / 60 into field "TestTime".
Leftover put statements write to the message window during play, such as put g_Level from the bank volume slider.
BANK09 aniplay would play p:\ecosim\master\bank5.flc; the file never shipped and is lost.
Also never called: MClick (old day-picker), SAVESCREEN (clipboard grab), edCheckComputer (startup checks), RandSound (street ambience).

traces.title: A licence key, redacted
traces.caption: The album's print tests register the PrintOMatic printing add-on with its licence key, written right into the scripts. It belongs to a third party, so the Studio notes that it is there and leaves it covered.

facts.text: printer(mRegister, "REDACTED") in ALBUM MovieScript 27, 28 and 31.

traces.title: Who saved what
traces.caption: Each movie file remembers who created it, who saved it last, and the folder it was saved to. Read together, they sketch the last weeks of production: most of the game passed through Alla's hands on its way to the QC folder, two files came from a backup folder, and one was last touched on the video station.

facts.text: ALBUM, FIELD, HOUSE2, HOUSE3, NEWS, STORE: last modified by "Alla - ", saved from P:\SECO\QC\.
BANK09 and SHARED: created by "alicia - edunetics", saved from Q:\ECOSIM\MOV_BACK\ (a backup folder).
INTRO: last modified by "Bennys - ". OPEN: last modified by "Video Station - Edunetics".
LOGIN: saved from N:\DIRECTOR.LIB\BOOKMARK\, the company Lingo library.

traces.title: BHOUSE1, the spare house
traces.caption: A backup copy of the first sod house sits on the disc, never installed and never opened by the game. It was last saved by "Bennys" on 30 May 1996, three weeks before the house that shipped. The differences are tiny: one moved bitmap, two narrower date fields, and the Mac font handling that came later. The credits list two Bennys, Benny Chukrun and Benny Tessler, and the file does not say which one.

facts.text: No Lingo, EXE string or SETUP.LST entry refers to BHOUSE1; SECO_CD.INF does not list it.
File dates: BHOUSE1 30 May 1996, HOUSE1 23 Jun 1996. BHOUSE1 saved from P:\SVIVOT\SECO\QC\ by "Bennys - ".
Only cast difference: 105-OLDMONY2.PCT (BHOUSE1) vs unnamed 104 (HOUSE1), pixel-identical.
HOUSE1 MovieScript 2 adds `if the machineType = 256` font handling for the Mac port; BHOUSE1 lacks it.

traces.title: The typo jar
traces.caption: Director never tidies its symbol table, so every slip of the keyboard typed into the message window is still there. They are the ordinary marks of people working fast and late, kept here with affection.

facts.text: retrun, puupetSprite, puppeetsprite, mouseDoun, moyuseDown, cleargloblas, updateStoge, firssttime, brith, MyObgect, plitical, g_Tatal
As shipped: Chech2, NuewLists, Nwespap, handaling, openning; a font called "New Times Roman".
Keyboard-mash test field in four movies: "ererererere / cvcvcvcvfdfd".

traces.title: freeBlock, freeBytes
traces.caption: Two little memory readouts from the town square, each wearing the other's label. The number is the same in both, so nobody ever noticed.

facts.text: TTALK/998-FBytes = "freeBlock 8634"; TTALK/999-FBlock = "freeBytes 8634".

traces.title: Neighbours on the disc
traces.caption: The installer was shared with other Edunetics titles and kept a line from one of them: if setup fails, try to install "the Map Room" again. The launcher hand-off kept a different kind of trace: the game asks for StudnetPrivatePath while the library offers StudentPrivatPath, so the two probably never met.

facts.text: MSCUISTF.DLL: "…try to install the Map Room again at a later time."
SHARED/CastScript 3282 - psApi asks for "StudnetPrivatePath"; XEDUAPI.DLL exposes StudentPrivatPath (inferred from strings, not tested).

traces.title: Fone
traces.caption: Two town-square sounds are named Fone and OFone. It might be the Russian word for "background". That is only a guess.

facts.text: OFone is byte-identical to DATA\SOUND\TTALK\TTALK1\TT1.WAV.

telegram.title: The first telegram
telegram.caption: The O'Grady rain-storm telegram was addressed, in the game's own data, to the lead software engineer, Alla. Before every player who ever lost a wagonload of wheat to a Kansas storm, there was the first one. (The credits spell her name LADIZANSKY; her test data says Ladizinsky. Both are shown as found.)

facts.text: BANK09/1014-Tel: TELEGRAM / FROM: O'Grady Town / TO: Alla Ladizinsky
Default bank name BANK09/1008-BankName = "Alla Lad"; CALEND/1091-ExName = "Alla Lad ". Both are overwritten with the player's name at run time.
FIELD/317-ALLA.PCT, a date-and-cash plate reading SEPT. 12 1880, is named after her too.

soundBooth.title: The 1894 strike
soundBooth.caption: Hi there, neighbour. I have bad news for you. My grain elevator is full, so I can't buy your grain. Because of the railroad strike, I can't ship the grain back east. Come back when the strike has finished.

soundBooth.title: The strike is over
soundBooth.caption: I have good news, neighbor! The railroad strike is over, and I have room in my grain elevator for your crops. I see that some of your grain went bad because you didn't have a good place to store it, but I'll be glad to buy the rest. Here are my prices.

soundBooth.title: Repaid on time
soundBooth.caption: Thank you for repaying your loan on time. I hope that we can do business with you again in the future.

soundBooth.title: Harriet: thank you for your order
soundBooth.caption: Thank you for paying for and placing your order. When your order arrives, I will deliver it to you.

studioNotes.a:
Dear Ma and Pa,

I'm sorry that it's taken so long for me to write. It took                                                                                                           me a long time to find a job. Before I found work, I ran                                                                                                      out of money and went into debt. Now I'm working
to pay off my debts, and I don't have a penny  to spare                                                                                                         at the end of the week.

I want to come back to the farm, where I belong, but I                                                                                                         need  your help. If you send me $200.00, I can pay off                                                                                                           my  debts and come home.

Your loving son,
